decisions.reason: Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT takes SV.SVSTDTC at VISITNUM=3, while adsl.r lines 115-126 take the earliest EX start date of a dosed EX record. The program computes the treatment start from a different source than the document states.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT substitutes the discontinuation date only when the final dose date is missing and the subject discontinued after visit 3; adsl.r lines 75-89 cap every EX end date of any non-completer at EOSDT (highest_imputation Y, including partial dates) with no visit 3 test. The program applies the imputation more broadly than the document states.

adsl.r lines 127-137 take the end date of the latest dosed EX record ordered by EXENDT and EXSEQ, which is the EX.EXENDTC of the subject's last EX record that Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT states. The two state the same logic.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE computes the planned dose as TRT01PN*TRTDUR, or for ARMN=2 as 54/81/54 mg per day over visit-dated intervals, while adsl.r lines 90-94 sum EXDOSE times each EX record's span. The program computes actual EX-based dose rather than the documented planned dose.

adsl.r line 148 builds AGEGR1 and AGEGR1N together from AGE through the specification codelist, so AGEGR1 is the decode paired with AGEGR1N as Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1 and ADSL.AGEGR1N state (<65, 65-80, >80). Deriving the pair in the other direction is the same grouping, not a different computation.

The quote truncates Define-XML ADSL.EFFFL, which requires an ADAS-Cog record and a CIBIC+ record with VISITNUM>3; adsl.r lines 162-165 filter ACTOT and CIBIC after visit 3 and line 181 requires both (effcnt == 2) with the SAFFL conditions. The two state the same logic.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL requires a visit 8 record and ENDDT >= the visit 8 date, while adsl.r lines 190-204 set Y for any WEEK 8 SV record and never compare an end date. The program omits the documented ENDDT condition.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL requires a visit 10 record and ENDDT >= the visit 10 date, while adsl.r lines 190-204 set Y for any WEEK 16 SV record and never compare an end date. The program omits the documented ENDDT condition.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL requires a visit 12 record and ENDDT >= the visit 12 date, while adsl.r lines 190-204 set Y for any WEEK 24 SV record and never compare an end date. The program omits the documented ENDDT condition.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL sets Y whenever the discontinuation reason is not Completed, while adsl.r line 61 also requires a nonmissing EOSDT and leaves subjects without a disposition record null. The program adds a condition the document does not state.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL tests DCREASCD ^= 'Completed', which the probe reads as the published DCSREAS bound to MT.ADSL.DCREASCD, and completers with a blank DCSREAS give the 110 Y-versus-blank differences. The DISCONFL__PROGRAM reading is labelled as the computation of adsl.r lines 53-61, which feed the final DISCONFL through the line 212 join, so it explains the reference without being offered as documentation.

Define-XML ADSL.DSRAEFL tests the coded discontinuation reason (DCREASCD='Adverse Event'), while adsl.r line 62 tests the verbatim DSTERM == "ADVERSE EVENT". The program reads a different variable than the document states.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN takes DS.VISITNUM of the DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED' record, while adsl.r lines 264-271 take the last SV visit below 100 by SVSTDTC. The program uses a different source than the document states, though both map 13 to 12.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN takes DS.VISITNUM only where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED', a term no record carries, so the literal probe is missing on all 254 records. The VISNUMEN__PROGRAM reading is labelled as the computation of adsl.r lines 264-271, which reach the final VISNUMEN through the line 283 join, so it explains the reference without being offered as documentation.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS is a grouping of DCDECOD values, while adsl.r line 230 overrides the DSDECOD grouping with "I/E Not Met" whenever DSTERM is "PROTOCOL ENTRY CRITERIA NOT MET". The program derives part of the value from DSTERM rather than DCDECOD.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT takes SV.SVSTDTC at VISITNUM=3, while adsl_v1.yaml EX_MINDTC (line 321) and TRTSDT take the earliest EX.EXSTDTC. No Visit 3 subject-visit selection appears anywhere in the composed specification.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT uses the discontinuation date only when the final dose date is missing and the subject discontinued after Visit 3. adsl_v1.yaml TRTEDT (lines 343-351) falls back to DS_DISP.DSSTDTC whenever LAST_EXENDTC is missing, with no discontinuation or Visit 3 condition, and DS_DISP can be a COMPLETED event.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE computes planned dose by ARMN group and visit-defined dosing intervals. adsl_v1.yaml CUMDOSE_BASE (line 375) and CUMDOSE instead sum EX.EXDOSE over each exposure record's study-day span, with no arm branches or visit boundaries.

Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1 derives the character group from ADSL.AGEGR1N. adsl_v1.yaml AGEGR1 (lines 463-469) derives it from DM.AGE and AGEGR1N is then mapped from AGEGR1, reversing the documented source.

Through AGEGR1 (adsl_v1.yaml lines 465-469) and the AGEGR1N mapping (lines 476-480), the specification applies the documented AGE <65, 65-80 and >80 intervals with codes 1, 2 and 3, so reading AGE through a helper is the same computation, not a different source. Only a missing AGE, which the otherwise branch would code 3, is treated differently, and that is not the difference this finding states.

Define-XML ADSL.RACEN's codelist CL.RACEN codes ASIAN as 7 and NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER as 5. The adsl_v1.yaml RACEN mapping (lines 496-501) lists only the other three races, and no other element of the composed specification codes them.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL compares ENDDT with the Visit 8 date, while adsl_v1.yaml COMP8FL (line 583) compares RFENDT. No retained section or workbook method defines ENDDT or equates it with RFENDT, so the specification's end-date source is not the documented one.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL compares ENDDT with the Visit 10 date, while adsl_v1.yaml COMP16FL (line 608) compares RFENDT. No retained section or workbook method defines ENDDT or equates it with RFENDT, so the specification's end-date source is not the documented one.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL compares ENDDT with the Visit 12 date, while adsl_v1.yaml COMP24FL (line 633) compares RFENDT. No retained section or workbook method defines ENDDT or equates it with RFENDT, so the specification's end-date source is not the documented one.
Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and workbook Methods row 106 name DISONSET, which no retained section defines. adsl_v1.yaml DURDIS_DAYS (lines 772-773) reads DISONSDT, an alias the documents never state.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN reads DS.VISITNUM from the record where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'. adsl_v1.yaml DS_VISITNUM (line 794) reads VISITNUM from DS_DISP, the lowest-DSSEQ DISPOSITION EVENT record, without that term condition.
Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT sums QS.QSORRES within MINI-MENTAL STATE. adsl_v1.yaml MMSETOT (line 810) sums QS.QSSTRESN, a different source column even where the numeric values agree.

Define-XML IT.ADSL.STUDYID (define-adam.xml lines 601-611) has Origin Type='Predecessor' DM.STUDYID, which documents the specification's copy; only the projected ADSL.STUDYID section omits it. The cited adsl.r lines 98-100 are program code and play no part in that documentation.

Define-XML IT.ADSL.USUBJID (define-adam.xml lines 612-622) has Origin Type='Predecessor' DM.USUBJID, which documents the specification's copy; only the projected ADSL.USUBJID section omits it. The cited adsl.r lines 98-100 are program code and play no part in that documentation.

Define-XML ADSL.SITEGR1 refers to SAP Section 7.1 without saying which sites are pooled, and no retained section supplies the criterion (the manifest marks the shared SAP pending_review). adsl.r lines 150-152 only call format_sitegr1 from an unretained package and in any case do not document the rule.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT states only conversion to a SAS date, and no retained section states the January and day-1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml TRTSDT (lines 330-331). ADRG page-8 and Define-XML ADAE.ASTDT state a partial-date convention only for AE start dates.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT and workbook Methods row 130 state only conversion of the final dose date to a SAS date, with no partial-date completion. No retained section states the January and day-1 completion of LAST_EXENDTC in adsl_v1.yaml TRTEDT (lines 355-357); the ADRG page-8 convention concerns ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.AVGDD states CUMDOSE/TRTDURD, a quotient with no value when TRTDURD is zero, and adsl_v2.yaml TRTDURD (line 216) copies the TRTDUR helper used as the denominator. The NULLIF guard in adsl_v1.yaml AVGDD_RAW (line 448) only leaves that undefined quotient missing, so it adds no distinct rule.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE and workbook Methods row 99 compute dose from visit-defined intervals and never count an open-ended last exposure record through TRTEDT. No retained section states the LAST_EX_DAYS rule in adsl_v1.yaml (lines 403-408).

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE and workbook Methods row 99 state dosing-interval formulas without completing partial exposure dates. No retained section states the January and day-1 completion of LAST_EXSTDTC in adsl_v1.yaml LAST_EXSTDTC_DT (lines 388-390); the ADRG page-8 convention is specific to ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE needs ARMN groups 0, 1 and 2, TRTDUR and TRTSTDT, which are not published ADSL variables, and no retained section defines them or the arm recoding. adsl.r lines 90-94 show a different computation of the reference and cannot fill the documented gap.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL needs ENDDT, which no retained section defines, so the date condition cannot be stated as a probe. adsl.r lines 193-203 compute the reference from the WEEK 8 visit alone and cannot document ENDDT.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL needs ENDDT, which no retained section defines, so the date condition cannot be stated as a probe. adsl.r lines 193-203 compute the reference from the WEEK 16 visit alone and cannot document ENDDT.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL needs ENDDT, which no retained section defines, so the date condition cannot be stated as a probe. adsl.r lines 193-203 compute the reference from the WEEK 24 visit alone and cannot document ENDDT.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL states WEIGHTBL / ((HEIGHTBL/100)**2), a quotient with no value when HEIGHTBL is zero. The NULLIF guard in adsl_v1.yaml BMIBL_RAW (line 709) only leaves that undefined quotient missing and otherwise implements the same formula, so it adds no distinct BMI rule.

Define-XML section ADSL.HEIGHTBL states only VSSTRESN when VS.VSTESTCD='HEIGHT' and VS.VISITNUM=1 and ADRG page-16 lists HEIGHTBL without a method, so no retained section chooses among several Visit 1 records, which the SDTM VS keys (define-sdtm.xml line 1954, with VSTPTNUM) allow. The order_by VS.VISITNUM and keep: first of adsl_v1.yaml BASE_HT (lines 115-118) is that unstated choice, and under the Visit 1 filter of adsl_v2.yaml (line 72) it leaves every qualifying record tied.

Define-XML section ADSL.WEIGHTBL states only VSSTRESN when VS.VSTESTCD='WEIGHT' and VS.VISITNUM=3 and ADRG page-16 lists WEIGHTBL without a method, so no retained section chooses among several Visit 3 records, which the SDTM VS keys (define-sdtm.xml line 1954, with VSTPTNUM) allow. The order_by VS.VISITNUM and keep: first of adsl_v1.yaml BASE_WT (lines 126-129) is that unstated choice, and under the Visit 3 filter of adsl_v2.yaml (line 75) it leaves every qualifying record tied.

SDTM Define-XML SC (define-sdtm.xml lines 1863-1870) declares one record per characteristic per subject with keys STUDYID, USUBJID, SCTESTCD. After the documented SCTESTCD=EDLEVEL selection, adsl_v1.yaml SC_EDU orders a single record, so keep: first adds no selection rule.

Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT and workbook Methods row 103 state conversion of the primary-diagnosis MHSTDTC to a SAS date without partial-date completion. No retained section states the January and day-1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml DISONSDT (lines 746-747); the ADRG page-8 convention concerns ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT selects MHCAT='PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS' but no record among several, and the SDTM MH keys STUDYID, USUBJID, MHTERM, MHSTDTC (define-sdtm.xml line 1518) allow several. No retained section states the lowest-MHSEQ choice in adsl_v1.yaml MH_DX (lines 213-216).

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and workbook Methods row 106 state only the number of months between two dates. No retained section states the inclusive day count (closed: both) in adsl_v1.yaml DURDIS_DAYS (lines 774-775).
Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and workbook Methods row 106 state months without a day-to-month conversion. No retained section supplies the 30.4375 divisor in adsl_v1.yaml DURDIS (line 780).

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS names DISONSET, which no retained section defines, and does not say how months are counted. The 30.4375-day month in adsl.r lines 285-300 shows how the reference was computed but does not document the rule.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDSGR1 groups DURDIS values as <12 and >=12 and says nothing of a missing duration. The otherwise branch of adsl_v1.yaml DURDSGR1 (line 789) also places a missing DURDIS in >=12, which no retained section states.

Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT and workbook Methods row 132 state conversion of the Visit 1 SVSTDTC to a SAS date only. No retained section states the January and day-1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml VISIT1DT (lines 762-763); ADRG page-8's partial-date statement concerns ADAE.ASTDT.

SDTM Define-XML SV (define-sdtm.xml lines 971-978) declares one record per actual visit per subject with keys STUDYID, USUBJID, VISITNUM. After the documented SV.VISITNUM=1 selection, adsl_v1.yaml SV1 orders a single record, so keep: first adds no tie-break rule.

Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT and workbook Methods row 117 state RFENDTC converted to a SAS date without partial-date completion. No retained section states the January and day-1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml RFENDT (lines 574-575); ADRG page-8's convention is limited to ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.DCDECOD selects DSCAT='DISPOSITION EVENT' without choosing among several such records, and the SDTM DS keys STUDYID, USUBJID, DSDECOD, DSSTDTC (define-sdtm.xml line 1439) allow several. No retained section states the lowest-DSSEQ choice in adsl_v1.yaml DS_DISP (lines 191-194).

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS describes grouping DCDECOD values and lists I/E Not Met as a category, but gives no DSTERM condition. No retained section or workbook method states the DSTERM='PROTOCOL ENTRY CRITERIA NOT MET' override in adsl_v1.yaml DCREASCD (line 669).

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS allows the coded value Completed and describes grouping completion status, without saying completers are left blank. No retained section or workbook method states the blank result for DCREASCD='Completed' in adsl_v2.yaml DCSREAS (lines 672-673).

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS and its CL.DISCREAS codelist list Sponsor Decision and Withdrew Consent as categories without pairing them with DCDECOD values. No retained section states the STUDY TERMINATED BY SPONSOR and WITHDRAWAL BY SUBJECT pairings in adsl_v1.yaml DC_REAS_MAP (lines 661-662).

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS describes grouping DCDECOD values and CL.DISCREAS lists categories, but no retained section maps each DCDECOD value, gives the I/E Not Met condition or says whether completers get Completed or a blank. adsl.r lines 222-230 compute the reference with an unretained format and do not document the mapping.

missed.quote: All patients in DM were included in ADSL.
missed.reason: ADRG page-11 states which records ADSL holds, but no claim cites it. The specification's row rule treated-subjects keeps only DM.ACTARM <> 'Screen Failure', following the 'Screen Failures are excluded' structure of Define-XML IG.ADSL (define-adam.xml line 182) rather than this statement.
